params.headline: Code in 8 weeks. No prior experience.
params.subheadline: A guided path from your first print() to a portfolio project

params.title: Learn by shipping, not by watching
params.subtitle: Every week ends with something you can show someone.

params.title: Why this course exists
params.body: Most Python courses dump syntax at you and call it teaching. We flip it: you build one small real thing per week — a quiz, a budget tracker, a tiny web scraper — and the syntax shows up exactly when you need it.

params.title: Cohorts over cramming
params.body: You're never alone. Every cohort has a live weekly call, a private channel, and a mentor who reviews your code within 24 hours.

params.title: The 20-minute rule
params.body: New concept? You watch a 3-minute explainer, then practice for 20 minutes in a real editor. If you're stuck longer than 20 minutes, you ping the cohort.

params.title: What you'll build
params.body: Week 1: a greeting script. Week 2: a quiz game. Week 3: a budget tracker. Week 4: a weather CLI. Week 5: data analysis on real CSV. Week 6: a web scraper. Week 7: an API. Week 8: your portfolio project, deployed.

params.definition: Code that follows the community's conventions — readable, Pythonic, and easy to maintain.
params.context: What mentors are always pushing you toward in reviews.
params.example: Using list comprehensions instead of clunky loops.

questions.q: Do I need any math background?
questions.a: No. If you can add two numbers, you have enough math for this course.
4-6 hours: one live call, three practice blocks, and the weekly build.
Lifetime access plus cohort catch-up weeks — you never miss the path.
Yes, with your deployed portfolio project as the real proof.

params.quote: I went from 'what is a variable?' to a deployed weather app in eight weeks. The builds made it stick.
params.author: Diego R.
